nodes.title: Residual monodromy at two primes is the full product
nodes.statement: Let l_1 ≠ l_2 be primes not dividing 2N with max(l_1, l_2) > 10, λ_i | l_i, and suppose each factor's geometric monodromy is the full group H_i ∈ {SL_n(k(λ_i)) (n > 2, −1 ∉ ⟨l_i⟩), SU_n(k(λ_i)) (n > 2, −1 ∈ ⟨l_i⟩), Sp_n(k(λ_i)) (self-dual data)}. Then for every t ∈ T_0(ℂ) the geometric monodromy π_1(T_0(ℂ), t) → H_1 × H_2 is surjective.
hypotheses: l_1 ≠ l_2 odd, prime to N, max(l_1, l_2) > 10 (in the self-dual case BLGHT11 needs only l_1, l_2 > 2 and residue fields ≠ 𝔽_3 for n = 2)
proofSteps: Each projection is surjective (DM.5/residual-monodromy-sl, DM.5/residual-monodromy-su, DM.5/residual-monodromy-sp).

The H_i are perfect with simple projective quotients, and no composition factor of H_2 is isomorphic to the simple quotient of H_1 when l_1 > 10 (DM.0/special-linear-unitary-simple, DM.0/artin-non-isomorphism); apply DM.0/product-of-simple-images.
acceptance: For Qian's switching (l, l′ with l′ ≡ 1 mod N, l′ > 2ln + 5 > 10) the hypotheses hold with H_2 = SL_n(𝔽_{l′}).

sources.locator: Proposition 3.8, first two paragraphs of the proof, p. 1261
sources.match: By Lemma 3.7, Goursat's lemma, the normal subgroups of SL_n and Artin's theorem, the monodromy surjects onto SL_n(k(𝔓_1)) × SL_n(k(𝔓_2)).
The symplectic analogue for square-free 𝔫 whose prime factors have distinct residue characteristics.
The product of SL_n and SU_n factors, by Lemma 5.2.3 and Goursat's lemma.

nodes.title: The level-structure torsors are geometrically irreducible
nodes.statement: Under the hypotheses of DM.5/two-prime-product-monodromy (and for one prime l ≡ 1 mod N), with level data as in DM.5/level-structure-torsor (pairings compatible with η_i in the unitary case; symplectic compatibility in the self-dual case), the scheme T({U_i}) is a smooth, geometrically irreducible F-variety. This is Qian's Proposition 3.8, BLGHT11 Proposition 4.2(1) with BLGGT14's correction, and BCGNT25 Proposition 4.4.2 with the compatibility proviso.
hypotheses: η_i compatible with the pairings in the unitary case (PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25/E23)
two primes with max > 10, or one prime l ≡ 1 mod N
proofSteps: T({U_i}) is finite étale over the smooth geometrically connected (T_0)_F, hence smooth; it is geometrically connected iff π_1(T_{0,ℚ̄}) acts transitively on a geometric fibre.
A geometric fibre is a torsor under ∏H_i (the groups preserving determinant and pairing), and the geometric monodromy surjects onto ∏H_i (DM.5/two-prime-product-monodromy), so it acts transitively.
A smooth connected variety over a field of characteristic 0 is irreducible.
acceptance: For one prime l ≡ 1 mod N with k(λ) = 𝔽_l, T(r̄_λ) is geometrically irreducible because the monodromy of W̄_λ is SL_n(𝔽_l) (BCGNT25 Remark 4.4.3).

sources.locator: Proposition 3.8 and the last paragraph of its proof, p. 1261
sources.match: T_W is geometrically connected, by transporting one point to another along a path whose monodromy is ψ_2ψ_1^{−1}.
T_W is geometrically connected for square-free 𝔫 with distinct residue characteristics.
T({U_{λ_i}}) is a geometrically irreducible smooth F-scheme; T(r̄_λ) likewise for one prime l ≡ 1 mod N.

nodes.title: Frobenius on the Fermat eigenlines is a product of Gauss sums
nodes.statement: Let F ⊇ ℚ(ζ_N), v a finite place of F of residue characteristic p ∤ Nl with residue field of q elements, ψ : 𝔽_q → ℚ̄_l^× a nontrivial additive character and t : μ_N(𝔽_q) ≅ μ_N(ℚ̄_l) the identification through the place. For a ∈ ℤ/Nℤ put g(v, a) = −∑_{x∈𝔽_q^×} t(x^{(1−q)/N})^a ψ(x) (so g(v, 0) = 1). Then for i ∈ B(a) the geometric Frobenius at v acts on the eigenline V_{λ,i} of the Fermat fibre by the scalar q^{−1}∏_{j=1}^N g(v, a_j + i), which is independent of ψ; for i ∉ B(a) the eigenspace is zero.
hypotheses: v ∤ Nl
geometric Frobenius on cohomology
proofSteps: The Fermat fibre has good reduction at v and the eigenspace decomposition commutes with Frobenius (DM.2/fermat-fibre-splitting).

Weil's computation of the zeta function of the Fermat hypersurface by Jacobi sums, written as products of Gauss sums (Deligne, Hodge cycles, §7, Proposition 7.10), gives the eigenvalue on each character line; ψ-independence follows because ∑_j(a_j + i) ≡ 0 mod N.
The Lefschetz trace formula over 𝔽_{q^m} for the elements of H identifies the eigenvalues.
acceptance: N = 3, the line with character (1, 1, 1) of the Fermat cubic: Frobenius acts by q^{−1}g(v, 1)³, which is a Jacobi sum of a cubic character up to sign, of complex absolute value √q.

sources.match: Frobenius acts on V_{λ,i} by q^{−1}∏_j g(v, a_j + i), with the Gauss sum defined through a fixed additive character, citing Deligne Proposition I.7.10.

sources.locator: Chapter I, §7, Proposition 7.10, as cited by QIAN23
sources.match: Frobenius eigenvalues on the character lines of the cohomology of Fermat hypersurfaces are products of Gauss sums.

nodes.title: Gauss-sum formula for the determinant of the Dwork motive
nodes.statement: For v ∤ Nl of odd residue characteristic with q = #k(v): det(Frob_v | V_{λ,0}) = q^{−n}∏_{b∈B}∏_{j=1}^{N} g(v, a_j + b) = q^{n(N−n−2)/2}(∏_{b∈B} g(v, b))^n. Equivalently ∏_{b∈B}∏_j g(v, a_j + b) = (∏_{b∈B} g(v, b))^n q^{n(N−1)/2 − n(n−1)/2}. By DM.5/determinant-descends this computes the character det V[λ] of G_F at Frob_v.
hypotheses: residue characteristic of v odd and prime to Nl (so (q − 1)/N is even)
proofSteps: For Qian's data the residues a_j + b (j = 1, …, N) run over b itself n + 1 times (from the n + 1 zeros) and over every s ≠ −b′, b′ ∈ B, at most once; regroup the double product as (∏g(v, b))^n · (∏_{s≠0}g(v, s))^n / ∏_{i≠j} g(v, b_j − b_i).
Use g(v, a)g(v, −a) = (−1)^{a(q−1)/N}q = q for a ≠ 0 (q − 1 even, N odd; Mathlib gaussSum_mul_gaussSum_eq_card) to evaluate ∏_{s≠0} g(v, s) = q^{(N−1)/2} and ∏_{i≠j} g(v, b_j − b_i) = q^{n(n−1)/2}.
Combine with the factor q^{−n} of DM.6/fermat-frobenius-gauss-sums.
acceptance: Weight check: |g(v, b)| = √q, so |det| = q^{n(N−n−2)/2}·q^{n²/2} = q^{n(N−2)/2}, consistent with purity of weight N − 2 in rank n.

sources.match: Rewrites the determinant of Frobenius on V_{λ,0} as (∏g(v, b_j))^n(q^{(N−1)/2})^n/q^{n(n−1)/2} times q^{−n}, using g(v, a)g(v, −a) = q for odd residue characteristic.

nodes.title: The Gauss-sum product descends to the cyclotomic coefficients
nodes.statement: For v ∤ Nl of residue characteristic p: ∏_{b∈B} g(v, b) ∈ ℚ_l(ζ_N). For the self-dual data with n = 2 (B = −B), g(v, b_1)g(v, b_2) ∈ ℚ_l(ζ_N)^+ = ℚ_l(ζ_N + ζ_N^{−1}).
hypotheses: ∑_{b∈B} b ≡ 0 mod N
for n = 2: B = −B
proofSteps: An automorphism σ of ℚ̄_l fixing ℚ_l(ζ_N) acts on p-th roots of unity by ζ_p ↦ ζ_p^a, a ∈ 𝔽_p^×; substituting x ↦ a^{−1}x gives σ(g(v, b)) = t(a^{(q−1)/N})^b g(v, b), and the product over B picks up t(a^{(q−1)/N})^{∑b} = 1.

For n = 2 let σ fix ℚ_l(ζ_N)^+; it acts on μ_N by ζ ↦ ζ^{±1} and on μ_p by some a; then σ(g(v, b)) = t(a^{(q−1)/N})^{±b}g(v, ±b), and the product over B = −B with b_1 + b_2 ≡ 0 is invariant. No σ fixing ζ_p need exist (the printed proof assumes one; PAPER-QIAN-23/E33).
acceptance: n = 2, l = 3, N = 301, p = 5: no σ ∈ G_{ℚ_3(ζ_N)^+} inverts ζ_N and fixes ζ_5, yet the argument above applies.

sources.locator: Proof of Lemma 3.9, equations (3.2) and (3.3), pp. 1263–1264
sources.match: Shows ∏g(v, b_j) ∈ ℚ_l(ζ_N) since ∑b_j ≡ 0, and for n = 2 that it lies in ℚ_l(ζ_N)^+ using B = −B.

nodes.title: The determinant of the residual Dwork motive is an n-th power up to 𝔽_{l²}
nodes.statement: Let F ⊇ ℚ(ζ_N) and λ a prime above l of O (of O^+ when n = 2), k(λ) its residue field. The character det V[λ] of G_F (DM.5/determinant-descends) takes values in (𝔽_{l²}^× k(λ)^×)^n ⊂ 𝔽̄_l^×; it takes values in (k(λ)^×)^n when 𝔽_{l²} ⊆ k(λ).
hypotheses: determinant read at t = 0
the factor q^{n(N−n−2)/2} is an n-th power after a quadratic coefficient extension when n is even
proofSteps: By Chebotarev it suffices to evaluate at Frobenius elements at v ∤ 2Nl; DM.6/dwork-determinant-gauss-formula gives q^{n(N−n−2)/2}(∏g(v, b))^n.
∏g(v, b) is λ-integral in ℚ_l(ζ_N) (resp. ℚ_l(ζ_N)^+) by DM.6/gauss-product-descent, so its reduction lies in k(λ).
q^{n(N−n−2)/2} = (q^{(N−n−2)/2})^n when N − n is even, and otherwise (√q)^{n(N−n−2)} with √q in 𝔽_{l²}.
acceptance: If l ≡ 1 mod N and n odd, the character takes values in (𝔽_l^×)^n.

sources.match: The determinant of V[λ] as a G_F-representation lands in (𝔽_{l²}^× k(λ)^×)^n.

nodes.title: Matching determinants at the coefficient prime l
nodes.statement: Let n = l^a m with l ∤ m, F a CM field, M = F(ζ_N), r̄ : G_F → GL_n(𝔽_{l^s}) continuous, and λ | l a prime of O (of O^+ when n = 2) whose residue field k(λ) contains 𝔽_{l²} and all m-th roots of all elements of 𝔽_{l^s}. Then (i) det r̄ takes values in (k(λ)^×)^n; (ii) det V[λ] (a character of G_M) takes values in (k(λ)^×)^n; (iii) the character det V[λ] ⊗ (det r̄|_{G_M})^{−1} takes values in (k(λ)^×)^n; (iv) μ_m(𝔽̄_l) ⊂ k(λ), so m | #k(λ)^× and the n-th power map on k(λ)^× has kernel μ_m. Hence ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4 (roots after a totally real base change) applies to this character with exponent m (the paper requires n | #k(λ)^× instead, which fails when l | n; PAPER-QIAN-23/E5).
hypotheses: k(λ) ⊇ 𝔽_{l²} and all m-th roots of elements of 𝔽_{l^s}
proofSteps: For x ∈ 𝔽_{l^s}^× pick y ∈ k(λ) with y^m = x; the l^a-th power map is bijective on k(λ)^×, so y = z^{l^a} and x = z^n.
DM.6/determinant-nth-power with 𝔽_{l²} ⊆ k(λ) gives (ii); (iii) follows; (iv) applies the hypothesis to x = 1.

A character with values in (k^×)^n = (k^×)^m (k^× cyclic of order prime to l) has an n-th root in k^× iff it has an m-th root; under the Teichmüller embedding this is the statement of ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.4/character-roots-after-base-change.
acceptance: n = l = 3, s = 1: m = 1, so every character into (k(λ)^×)^3 = k(λ)^× already has a cube root, and the condition n | #k(λ)^× of the published text would wrongly fail.

sources.locator: §4, paragraph beginning 'On the side of characteristic l', p. 1270, with Lemma 3.9
sources.match: Applies Lemma 3.9 over F(ζ_N) to see that det V[λ] ⊗ (det r̄)^∨ has image in (k(λ)^×)^n, under conditions on N giving 𝔽_{l²} and the m-th roots inside k(λ).
n-th roots of (𝔽_{l^r}^×)^n-valued characters after a totally real base change avoiding a given field; the atlas plans it in ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4.

nodes.title: Matching determinants at the auxiliary prime l′ ≡ 1 mod N
nodes.statement: Let l′ be an odd prime with l′ ≡ 1 mod N and λ′ | l′ a prime of O (of O^+ when n = 2), so k(λ′) = 𝔽_{l′} and ℚ(ζ_N)_{λ′} = ℚ_{l′}. For v ∤ 2Nl′ with q = #k(v) and geometric Frobenius Frob_v: (i) det(Frob_v | V_{λ′,0})·q^{−n(n−1)/2} = (q^{(N−2n−1)/2}∏_{b∈B} g(v, b))^n, with q^{(N−2n−1)/2}∏g(v, b) ∈ ℤ_{l′}^×; equivalently det V_{λ′} ⊗ ε_{l′}^{n(n−1)/2} takes the value (q^{(N−2n−1)/2}∏g(v, b))^n at Frob_v. (ii) Hence for every continuous r̄′ : G_F → GL_n(𝔽_{l′}) with det r̄′ = ε̄_{l′}^{−n(n−1)/2}, the character (det r̄′|_{G_M})^{−1} ⊗ det V[λ′] takes values in (𝔽_{l′}^×)^n. (iii) If moreover l′ ≡ 1 mod n, then μ_n ⊂ 𝔽_{l′} and ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4 applies with exponent n. The printed argument uses the statement of Lemma 3.9 (values only in (𝔽_{l′²}^×)^n) and the sign det r̄′ = ε̄^{+n(n−1)/2}; the cancellation in (i), the sign and the congruence l′ ≡ 1 mod n are the corrections PAPER-QIAN-23/E6, E9, E7.
hypotheses: l′ ≡ 1 mod N (and mod n for (iii))
ε_{l′}^{−1}(Frob_v) = q for geometric Frobenius
proofSteps: (i) is a rearrangement of DM.6/dwork-determinant-gauss-formula: q^{n(N−n−2)/2}·q^{−n(n−1)/2} = (q^{(N−2n−1)/2})^n, with N odd making the exponent an integer; the base is an l′-adic unit because |g(v, b)|_{l′} = 1 for v ∤ l′.
ε_{l′}^{−n(n−1)/2}(Frob_v) = q^{n(n−1)/2}, so (det r̄′)^{−1} cancels the remaining power of q; the reduction of the base lies in 𝔽_{l′}.
μ_n ⊂ 𝔽_{l′} when l′ ≡ 1 mod n; such primes with l′ ≡ 1 mod Nn have positive density.
acceptance: For r̄′ = Sym^{n−1} r̄_{E_0,l′} with r̄_{E_0,l′} = H¹_ét(E_0, 𝔽_{l′}) (determinant ε̄^{−1}) the hypothesis det r̄′ = ε̄^{−n(n−1)/2} holds.

sources.locator: §4, paragraph beginning 'On the other side of characteristic l′', p. 1270; Lemma 3.9 and (3.1), pp. 1262–1263
sources.match: Applies Lemma 3.9 at λ′ to the character (det Sym^{n−1}r̄_{E,l′})^∨ ⊗ det V[λ′], with the corrections recorded as E6, E7 and E9.

nodes.title: Frobenius polynomials of Dwork fibres are integral and independent of λ
nodes.statement: Let F/ℚ(ζ_N) be a number field, v a finite place of F of residue characteristic l′ ∤ N, and t ∈ T_0(O_{F_v}). For every place λ of M of residue characteristic ≠ l′, W_{t,λ} (and V_{t,λ}) is unramified at v, and Q_v(X) = det(X − Frob_v | W_{t,λ}) has coefficients in O_M and is independent of λ.
hypotheses: t ∈ T_0(O_{F_v}), i.e. t integral with t^N − 1 a unit (good reduction)
proofSteps: Y_t is smooth and proper over O_{F_v}; smooth proper base change makes H^{N−2}_ét(Y_{t,F̄_v}, O_{M_λ}) unramified and identifies it with the cohomology of the special fibre.

Katz–Messing (for every h ∈ H_0, the characteristic polynomial of h·Frob on cohomology has coefficients in a fixed number field, independent of λ) applied to the projector e_χ gives λ-independence for V_{t,λ}; twisting by Ψ_λ^{−1}, which is λ-independent (DM.3/twisting-hecke-character), gives it for W_{t,λ}.

Integrality of Q_v: W_{t,λ} is an O_{M_λ}-lattice for every λ ∤ l′, so Q_v has λ-integral coefficients for all such λ; at λ | l′ use the crystalline comparison of DM.7/crystalline-at-good-reduction, where the published deduction from the untwisted polynomial does not transfer through the Ψ-twist (PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25/E24).
acceptance: deg Q_v = n and the roots of Q_v have complex absolute value q_v^{(n−1)/2} (purity of weight n − 1).

sources.locator: Proposition 4.2.5(1) and proof, published pp. 37–38 (arXiv v3 p. 42)
sources.match: W_{t,λ} is unramified at v and Q_v has coefficients in O_M independent of λ, by smooth proper base change and Katz–Messing Theorem 2(2).
For a smooth projective variety over a finite field with a finite group action, characteristic polynomials of h·Frob on ℓ-adic cohomology have integral coefficients independent of ℓ.

nodes.title: Twisted de Rham eigenspaces of the Dwork family
nodes.statement: Let H_dR = H^{N−2}_dR(Y/(T_0 × ℚ(ζ_N))), locally free with Hodge filtration F^j by local direct summands. For σ ∈ Gal(ℚ(ζ_N)/ℚ) put H_{dR,σ} = H_dR ⊗_{σ^{−1}, ℚ(ζ_N)} ℚ(ζ_N) (the right factor viewed as coefficients) and V_{dR,σ} = e_χ H_{dR,σ}, the χ-eigensheaf for H_0 acting through the coefficients, with filtration F^jV_{dR,σ} and graded pieces gr^j. At t = 0, V_{dR,σ,0} = ⊕_{i} V_{dR,σ,i} under the characters χ_i of H. For a finite extension K/ℚ(ζ_N)_v, t ∈ T_0(K) and an embedding σ : K ↪ ℚ̄_l = \overline{ℚ(ζ_N)_λ}, the de Rham comparison gives an isomorphism of filtered vector spaces ((V_{λ,t} ⊗ ℚ(ζ_N)_λ) ⊗_{σ,K} B_dR)^{G_K} ≅ V_{dR,σ|ℚ(ζ_N), t} ⊗_{K,σ} ℚ(ζ_N)_λ: the twist by σ matches the embedding of the local field with the embedding of the coefficients.
hypotheses: characteristic 0 base T_0 × ℚ(ζ_N)
λ and v of the same residue characteristic l
proofSteps: Relative Hodge bundles of a smooth proper family in characteristic 0 are locally free, the Hodge spectral sequence degenerates and character idempotents cut out locally free summands with the induced filtration (ComplexComparisonPartII C5).
The filtered de Rham comparison for proper smooth varieties over p-adic fields (CohomologyComparisons CP.3) is H_0-equivariant; taking χ-parts introduces the twist by σ.
acceptance: For σ = id and t = 0, V_{dR,id,0} = ⊕_{i∈B} V_{dR,i} with one-dimensional summands.

sources.locator: §3, notation for relative de Rham cohomology preceding Lemma 3.9 (published Lemma 3.10), pp. 1264–1265
sources.match: Defines H_dR, its σ-twists, the χ-eigenspaces V_{dR,σ} with filtration and graded pieces, the decomposition at t = 0 and the de Rham comparison with the twist.

sources.locator: §5, the spaces U_{DR,σ} and the comparison, pp. 34–35
sources.match: The self-dual analogue, with coefficients embeddable in the field containing t but no canonical embedding.

nodes.title: Hodge grades of the Fermat eigenlines
nodes.statement: Write σ^{−1}(ζ_N) = ζ_N^a and ⟨x⟩ for the representative of x mod N in {1, …, N}. Then V_{dR,σ,i} ≠ 0 iff i ∈ B, it is then one-dimensional, and its only nonzero graded piece is in degree M(a) + #{b ∈ B : ⟨ab⟩ < ⟨ai⟩}, where M(a) = (∑_j⟨a·a_j + 1⟩)/N − 1; equivalently the degree is (∑_j⟨a(a_j + i)⟩)/N − 1. For the self-dual data (BLGHT11 Lemma 5.2(1)) the degree is (N − n − 3)/2 + #{b ∈ B : ⟨ab⟩ ≤ ⟨ai⟩}.
hypotheses: a ∈ (ℤ/Nℤ)^× determined by σ
proofSteps: After base change along τ_0σ^{−1} to ℂ, gr^jV_{dR,σ,i} is the eigenspace of H^{j, N−2−j}(Y_0(ℂ)) for the character (a(a_j + i))_j of H.
DM.2/fermat-hypersurface-cohomology: nonzero iff all a(a_j + i) ≢ 0 (i.e. i ∈ B), in Hodge degree j with j + 1 = ∑⟨a(a_j + i)⟩/N.
Set j(d) = ∑⟨a·a_j + d⟩/N − 1; it increases by one when passing d ≡ ab, b ∈ B, and is constant otherwise; induct from M(a) = j(1).
acceptance: For σ = id (a = 1) and Qian's datum with n = 3, the three lines i = 1, 2, N − 3 have consecutive grades M(1), M(1) + 1, M(1) + 2.

sources.locator: Lemma 3.10(1) and its proof, p. 1266 (arXiv v1 Lemma 3.9(1))
sources.match: Computes the unique nonzero graded piece of each Fermat eigenline from Deligne's Propositions I.7.4 and I.7.6.
The self-dual analogue.

nodes.title: Consecutive Hodge numbers of the Dwork motives
nodes.statement: For each σ, gr^jV_{dR,σ} is locally free of rank one on T_0 × ℚ(ζ_N) for M(a) ≤ j ≤ M(a) + n − 1 and zero otherwise; V_{dR,σ} is locally free of rank n. For the self-dual data the range is (N − 1 − n)/2 ≤ j ≤ (N + n − 3)/2 (BLGHT11 Lemma 5.2(2)).
hypotheses: Hodge numbers are locally constant in a smooth proper family in characteristic 0
proofSteps: gr^jV_{dR,σ} is locally free (DM.7/twisted-de-rham-eigenspaces), so its rank can be computed at t = 0.
At t = 0 the grades of the n eigenlines are M(a) + #{b : ⟨ab⟩ < ⟨ai⟩}, which run through M(a), …, M(a) + n − 1 as i runs through B ordered by ⟨ai⟩ (DM.7/hodge-grades-of-fermat-eigenlines).
acceptance: Every gr^j has rank ≤ 1: the Dwork motives have regular (multiplicity-free) Hodge numbers.

sources.locator: Lemma 3.10(2) and the last paragraph of its proof, p. 1266
sources.match: gr^jV_{dR,σ} is locally free of rank one exactly for M(a) ≤ j ≤ M(a) + n − 1.
The self-dual range.

nodes.title: Dwork fibres are de Rham with consecutive labelled Hodge–Tate weights
nodes.statement: Let v | l be a place of F ⊇ ℚ(ζ_N) and t ∈ T_0(F_v). (1) V_{λ,t} ⊗ ℚ(ζ_N)_λ is a de Rham representation of G_{F_v} (not of G_F; PAPER-QIAN-23/E8), and for an embedding σ : F_v ↪ ℚ̄_l with σ^{−1}(ζ_N) = ζ_N^a on ℚ(ζ_N), its σ-labelled Hodge–Tate weights (cohomological convention) are M(a), M(a) + 1, …, M(a) + n − 1, each with multiplicity one. (2) W_{t,λ} is de Rham with HT_σ(W_{t,λ}) = {0, 1, …, n − 1} for every σ. (3) For the self-dual data V_{λ,t}((N − 1 − n)/2) is de Rham with Hodge–Tate numbers {0, …, n − 1} at every embedding (BLGHT11 Lemma 5.3(1)).
hypotheses: l the residue characteristic of λ and v
proofSteps: (1) is DM.7/twisted-de-rham-eigenspaces with DM.7/consecutive-hodge-numbers.
(2): W_{t,λ} = V_{t,λ} ⊗ Ψ_λ^{−1} has weights shifted by a constant M′_σ; det W_λ ≅ M_λ(n(1 − n)/2) (DM.3/twisted-dwork-local-system) gives nM′_σ + n(n − 1)/2 = n(n − 1)/2, so M′_σ = 0.
(3) as in (1) with the Tate twist.
acceptance: For n = 3 and every embedding, the weights of W_{t,λ} are {0, 1, 2}.

sources.locator: Lemma 3.11(1), pp. 1266–1267, with the comparison on p. 1265 (correction E8)
sources.match: V_{λ,t} is de Rham with σ-labelled Hodge–Tate weights M(a), …, M(a) + n − 1.
W_{t,λ} is de Rham with HT_τ = {0, …, n − 1}, by Qian's lemma and the determinant.
Hodge–Tate numbers {0, …, n − 1} of V_{λ,t}((N − 1 − n)/2).

nodes.title: Crystallinity and Frobenius at good-reduction fibres
nodes.statement: Let v | l, l ∤ N, and t ∈ O_{F_v} with t^N − 1 a unit. Then V_{λ,t} and W_{t,λ} are crystalline representations of G_{F_v}; the characteristic polynomial of Frob_v on WD(W_{t,λ}) equals Q_v(X) of the special fibre (the same polynomial as for λ′ ∤ l, DM.6/frobenius-polynomials-independent); and W_{t,λ} is ordinary iff the roots of Q_v in ℚ̄_l have l-adic valuations 0, f, 2f, …, (n − 1)f, f = [k(v) : 𝔽_l]. No crystallinity is claimed at the punctures or for t merely integral. For the self-dual data, V_{λ,t}((N − 1 − n)/2) is crystalline under the same condition (BLGHT11 Lemma 5.3(2)).
hypotheses: l ∤ N
proofSteps: Y_t has good reduction over O_{F_v}; the crystalline comparison theorem gives crystallinity of H^{N−2}_ét and an H_0- and Frobenius-equivariant identification of D_cris with crystalline cohomology of the special fibre; Ψ_λ is crystalline at v.
The characteristic polynomial of φ^f on the twisted χ-part of crystalline cohomology equals Q_v by Katz–Messing (applicable to crystalline cohomology by Gillet–Messing).
Regular consecutive weights {0, …, n − 1} and the slope criterion for ordinarity (PadicHodgeTheory R06.2) give the last statement.
acceptance: If the special fibre point x has Q_x with l-adic slopes 0, 1, …, n − 1 (normalised), W_{t,λ} is crystalline ordinary.

sources.match: For t ∈ O_{F_v} with t^N − 1 ∉ 𝔪, V_{λ,t} is crystalline because Y_t has good reduction.
Crystallinity, the Frobenius characteristic polynomial Q_v via Katz–Messing and Gillet–Messing, and the slope criterion for ordinarity (Geraghty Lemma 2.32).
Crystallinity of the self-dual fibres at good reduction.

nodes.title: Ordinarity of fibres near the Fermat point when l ≡ 1 mod N
nodes.statement: Let l ≡ 1 mod N (so ℚ(ζ_N)_λ = ℚ_l), v | l and t ∈ 𝔪_{F_v}. Then V_{λ,t} is ordinary of weight μ with μ_{σ,i} = M(a_σ) for all i (in the convention of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.0, cohomological weights M(a_σ), …, M(a_σ) + n − 1), where σ^{−1}(ζ_N) = ζ_N^{a_σ}. For the self-dual data, V_{λ,t}((N − 1 − n)/2) is ordinary of weight 0, and its reduction at t = 0 is 𝔽_l ⊕ 𝔽_l(−1) ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ 𝔽_l(1 − n) as a module for inertia (BLGHT11 Lemma 5.3(3)–(4)).
hypotheses: l ≡ 1 mod N
t ∈ 𝔪_{F_v}
proofSteps: For t ∈ 𝔪_{F_v}, Y_t and Y_0 have the same special fibre, so D_cris(V_{λ,t}) ≅ D_cris(V_{λ,0}) as φ-modules (crystalline comparison); their labelled Hodge–Tate weights agree (DM.7/dwork-hodge-tate-weights).
By the slope criterion (PadicHodgeTheory R06.2, the crystalline form of BLGHT Lemma 2.2), V_{λ,t} is ordinary iff V_{λ,0} is.

V_{λ,0} ⊗ ℚ̄_l = ⊕_{i∈B} V_{λ,i}, each a crystalline character of G_{ℚ_l(ζ_N)_v} = G_{ℚ_l} with Hodge–Tate weight M(a_σ) + #{b : ⟨a_σb⟩ < ⟨a_σi⟩}, so as an inertia module it is ⊕_{i=0}^{n−1} ℚ̄_l(−M(a_σ) − i): an ordinary filtration.
acceptance: For the self-dual data and l ≡ 1 mod N the inertia action on the Fermat fibre mod λ is 𝔽_l ⊕ 𝔽_l(−1) ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ 𝔽_l(1 − n) (after the Tate twist).

sources.locator: Lemma 3.11(3) and its proof, pp. 1266–1267 (using Lemma 2.4)
sources.match: For l ≡ 1 mod N and t ∈ 𝔪_{F_v}, V_{λ,t} is ordinary of weight (M(a_σ)), by comparison with the Fermat fibre.
The self-dual analogue, ordinary of weight 0, and the inertia action on the Fermat fibre mod λ.

nodes.title: Inertia on the Fermat fibre when l ≡ −1 mod N
nodes.statement: Let l > n be prime with l ≡ −1 mod N, v a place of ℚ(ζ_N) and λ a place of M above l, τ, cτ : k(v) → k(λ) = 𝔽_{l²} the two isomorphisms, and ω_τ = τ ∘ Art^{−1} the fundamental character of level two on inertia. Then W̄_{0,λ} ≅ ⊕_{i=1}^n ω_τ^{i−1}ω_{cτ}^{n−i} as representations of I_{ℚ(ζ_N)_v}. For the self-dual data, V[λ]((N − 1 − n)/2)_0 ⊗ 𝔽̄_l is the analogous sum of n distinct level-two characters (BLGHT11 Lemma 5.3(5)).
hypotheses: l ≡ −1 mod N, l > n
ω_τ is defined only on inertia
proofSteps: H extends the H_0-action on the Fermat fibre and decomposes W̄_{0,λ} into n lines W̄_{0,λ,j}, the Ψ^{−1}-twists of the H-eigenspaces in H^{N−2} (printed H^{N−1}, PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25/E9), each crystalline of rank one.
The skew-Hermitian pairing (DM.5/hermitian-poincare-pairing) is orthogonal for this decomposition, so W̄_{0,λ,j}^c ≅ W̄_{0,λ,j}^∨ε̄^{1−n}.
Ordering so that HT_τ(W_{0,λ,j}) = j − 1, Fontaine–Laffaille (l > n) gives W̄_{0,λ,j} ≅ ω_τ^{j−1}ω_{cτ}^{a_j}, and the duality forces a_j = n − j.
acceptance: n = 2: W̄_{0,λ}|_I ≅ ω_{cτ} ⊕ ω_τ, the restriction to inertia of the induction of a level-two fundamental character.

sources.locator: Lemma 4.4.4 and proof, published pp. 42–43 (arXiv v3 p. 48)
sources.match: Identifies the inertial action on W̄_{0,λ} with ⊕ω_τ^{i−1}ω_{cτ}^{n−i} using the H-eigenspace decomposition of the Fermat fibre and the pairing.
The self-dual analogue for l ≡ −1 mod N.

nodes.title: Maximal unipotent local monodromy at places with v(t) < 0
nodes.statement: Let v be a finite place of F ⊇ ℚ(ζ_N) and λ′ a prime of residue characteristic l′ ≠ char(v), l′ odd and prime to N. (1) If t ∈ O_{F_v} and t^N − 1 is a unit, V_{λ′,t} is unramified at v. (2) If v(t) < 0, V_{λ′,t}|_{G_{F_v}} is tamely ramified, inertia acts unipotently through exp(t_{l′}(σ)N) and the monodromy operator N of its Weil–Deligne representation has minimal polynomial X^n (a single Jordan block); for the self-dual data a Frobenius lift has characteristic polynomial (X − α)(X − αq)⋯(X − αq^{n−1}) with α = ±1 (after the twist (N − 1 − n)/2), i.e. WD is an unramified twist of Steinberg (BLGHT11 Lemma 5.1). The hypothesis v(t) < 0 is necessary (PAPER-QIAN-23/E1).
hypotheses: l′ ≠ residue characteristic of v
proofSteps: (1) is smooth proper base change.

(2): near t = ∞ the family over the punctured disc {v(t) < 0} has geometric monodromy generated by the local monodromy at ∞, which is a single unipotent Jordan block over ℚ̄_{l′} (DM.4/maximal-unipotent-monodromy-at-infinity, applied to every conjugate character).

The Galois action of G_{F_v} on the fibre at t factors through the local fundamental group of the punctured disc at ∞ (tame specialisation of nearby cycles); inertia maps to the d-th power of the local monodromy generator, d = −v(t) > 0, still a single unipotent block in characteristic 0 (the argument of HSBT10 Lemma 1.15(2)).
For the Frobenius eigenvalues, the weight filtration of a single Jordan block and purity of the special value at ∞ give the Steinberg shape (BLGHT11).
acceptance: For the self-dual data with n = 2 and v(t) < 0, V_{λ′,t} is an unramified twist of the Steinberg representation at v, as for an elliptic curve with multiplicative reduction.

sources.locator: Lemma 3.12 and its proof, pp. 1267–1268, with correction E1
sources.match: The monodromy operator of WD(V_{λ′,t}|G_{F_v}) has minimal polynomial X^n, following Harris–Shepherd-Barron–Taylor Lemma 1.15(2); the hypothesis v(t) < 0 must be added.
Unramified for integral t with t^N − 1 a unit; tamely ramified with a single unipotent Jordan block and Steinberg-shaped Frobenius for t ∉ O_F.

nodes.title: The Dwork fibres form weakly compatible systems
nodes.statement: Let F/ℚ(ζ_N) be a number field, t ∈ T_0(F) and S the finite places v with v | N or t ∉ T_0(O_{F_v}). Then (M, S, {Q_v(X)}_{v∉S}, {W^{ss}_{t,λ}}_λ, {{0, 1, …, n − 1}}_τ) is a weakly compatible system of l-adic representations of G_F over M of rank n, pure of weight n − 1 (BLGGT14 §5.1); the same holds for {V_{t,λ}} with Hodge–Tate multisets {M(a_τ), …, M(a_τ) + n − 1} and for the self-dual data over M^+ (with symplectic pairings).
proofSteps: Away from S and the residue characteristic of λ, W_{t,λ} is unramified with Frobenius polynomial Q_v independent of λ (DM.6/frobenius-polynomials-independent).

At v | l with v ∉ S, W_{t,λ} is crystalline with Hodge–Tate weights {0, …, n − 1} and the same Frobenius polynomial (DM.7/crystalline-at-good-reduction, DM.7/dwork-hodge-tate-weights); at every v | l it is de Rham.
Purity of weight n − 1 is Deligne's theorem for the smooth fibres twisted by Ψ of weight N − n − 1.
acceptance: deg Q_v = n, Q_v(0) = ± q_v^{n(n−1)/2}, as the determinant ε^{−n(n−1)/2} requires.

sources.match: The family (M, S, {Q_v}, {W^{ss}_{t,λ}}, {{0, …, n − 1}}) is a weakly compatible system of rank n, pure of weight n − 1, in the sense of BLGGT14 §5.1.
Definition of weakly compatible systems of l-adic representations.

nodes.title: Generic slopes of indecomposable lisse sheaves (Drinfeld–Kedlaya)
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth irreducible variety over a finite field of characteristic p and E a lisse ℚ̄_{l′}-sheaf of rank n on X (l′ ≠ p) which is algebraic (Frobenius characteristic polynomials with algebraic coefficients). Fix a p-adic valuation on ℚ̄ and for x ∈ |X| let a^x_1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ a^x_n be the p-adic slopes of Frob_x normalised by deg x. (i) There are rational numbers a^η_1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ a^η_n such that the set U of x with a^x_i = a^η_i for all i is nonempty and meets every curve in an open set; (ii) ∑_{i≤r} a^x_i ≤ ∑_{i≤r} a^η_i for all x, r; (iii) if E is indecomposable then a^η_i − a^η_{i+1} ≤ 1 for 1 ≤ i < n.
hypotheses: E algebraic; (iii) requires E indecomposable (e.g. geometrically irreducible)
proofSteps: Drinfeld–Kedlaya prove the corresponding statement for indecomposable convergent or overconvergent F-isocrystals (their Theorem 1.1.5) and transport it to lisse sheaves using Abe's crystalline companions (their §5).
(ii) is Grothendieck's specialisation theorem for Newton polygons.
acceptance: For E pure of weight n − 1 with slopes 0, 1, …, n − 1 at one point, (ii) and (iii) force the generic slopes to be 0, 1, …, n − 1.

sources.locator: Theorem 1.3.3, pp. 4–5 (arXiv v11); proof in §5, pp. 11–12
sources.match: For an algebraic lisse sheaf on a smooth variety over a finite field, generic slopes exist and are attained on a dense set, special slopes lie above generic ones, and for indecomposable sheaves consecutive generic slopes differ by at most one.
Applies DK17 Theorem 1.3.3 to the lisse sheaf W_μ with λ-adic slopes.

nodes.title: Generic crystalline ordinarity of the Dwork family
nodes.statement: Let v be a place of ℚ(ζ_N) of residue characteristic l ∤ N and λ a place of M of the same characteristic. There is a nonempty Zariski open U(v; λ) ⊂ T_{0,k(v)} such that for every finite extension F_w/ℚ(ζ_N)_v and every t ∈ T_0(O_{F_w}) whose reduction lies in U(v; λ)(k(w)), W_{t,λ} is a crystalline ordinary representation of G_{F_w}.
hypotheses: l ∤ N
Qian's datum, n > 2 (BCGNT25 setting)
proofSteps: By DM.7/crystalline-at-good-reduction it suffices that the normalised l-adic slopes s_1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ s_n of Q_x (computed with an auxiliary μ of residue characteristic ≠ l) be n − 1, …, 1, 0 for x ∈ U.

W_μ is geometrically irreducible (DM.3/twisted-dwork-local-system); Drinfeld–Kedlaya (DM.7/drinfeld-kedlaya-slope-bound) give a dense open V with constant slopes and gaps ≤ 1; with ∑s_i = n(n − 1)/2 (determinant) it suffices to find U ⊂ V with s_n(x) = 0.

By (4.2.3) and the trace formula of E_μ (DM.3/hypergeometric-sheaf-properties), s_n(x) = 0 when tr(Frob_x | E_{μ,x}) ≢ 0 mod λ. Writing ρ_i through z ↦ z^{c_i}, the trace is congruent to N_{k/k(v)}(u(x)) for the polynomial u(T) = ∑_r(−1)^{nr}∏_i C(c_i, r)T^r (Lucas's theorem; one exponent in the printed proof is misprinted, PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25/E8); take U = T_{1,k(v)}[1/u] pulled back, nonempty since u(0) = 1.
acceptance: The open set is independent of the extension k/k(v): u has coefficients in k(v).

sources.locator: Proposition 4.2.6 and proof, published pp. 38–40 (arXiv v3 pp. 43–45)
sources.match: Proves generic crystalline ordinarity by Drinfeld–Kedlaya, the determinant and a computation of the hypergeometric trace modulo λ following DK17 §A.3.

sources.locator: Appendix A, §A.3 (Proposition A.3.1, Corollary A.3.2) (arXiv v11)
sources.match: The key computation of the slopes of the hypergeometric sheaves E_c.

nodes.title: The equivariant semistable blowup of the reciprocal Dwork family
nodes.statement: Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p ∤ N, W = W(k), and Spec W[T, U^{±1}]′ the open where (TU)^N ≠ 1. Let Y_N ⊂ ℙ^{N−1} × Spec W[T, U^{±1}]′ be UT(X_1^N + ⋯ + X_N^N) = N X_1⋯X_N (the Dwork family in the reciprocal parameter s = 1/t = UT), with D_i = {X_i = 0} and D = {∑X_i^N = 0}. Blow up D ∩ D_N, then successively the intersections of the strict transforms of D and D_j for j = N − 1, …, 1. The result 𝕏 satisfies: (a) every centre is H_0-stable, so H_0 acts on 𝕏 and the blowdown 𝕏 → Y_N is H_0-equivariant; (b) the blowdown is an isomorphism over T ≠ 0; (c) étale locally 𝕏 is étale over W[T, U^{±1}]′[Z_1, …, Z_r, Z_{r+1}^{±1}, …, Z_m^{±1}]/(TU − Z_1⋯Z_r), H_0-equivariantly with H_0 acting on the Z_i by characters. Base change along T ↦ π, U ↦ u (u ∈ O_F^×) gives a semistable model with H_0-action of uπ(∑X_i^N) = N∏X_i over O_F; base change to ℂ along U ↦ 1 gives a blowup of T(∑X_i^N) = N∏X_i over 𝔸¹ − μ_N, an isomorphism away from T = 0, whose fibre over 0 is a reduced normal crossings divisor without self-crossings.
hypotheses: p ∤ N
semistable: reduced normal crossings special fibre without self-intersections
proofSteps: The successive blowup centres are intersections of H_0-stable divisors, hence H_0-stable; blowups commute with flat base change.
Compute charts after each blowup by hand (QIAN21 pp. 5–8): the local equation becomes TU = Z_1⋯Z_r times a unit.
Remark 2.2 of QIAN21 records the H_0-equivariant charts.
acceptance: For N = 3 the fibre of Y_N over T = 0 is the triangle X_1X_2X_3 = 0 (three lines), already a reduced normal crossings divisor; the blowups resolve the singular points of the total space where D meets the coordinate lines.

sources.locator: Lemma 2.1, Remark 2.2 and the paragraph after it, pp. 4–8 (arXiv v1)
sources.match: Constructs the H_0-equivariant blowup of UT(∑X_i^N) = N∏X_i with semistable étale-local charts.
Uses the base change of this blowup to ℂ, whose fibre over 0 is a reduced normal crossings divisor.

nodes.title: Equivariant semistable models of Dwork fibres near infinity
nodes.statement: Let F/ℚ_p be finite containing ζ_N, p ∤ N, π a uniformiser, and t ∈ F with v(t) = d > 0 (the fibre at s = t, i.e. Dwork parameter t^{−1}). Then there are e ≥ 1 and a strictly semistable model 𝒴 over O_{F′}, F′ = F(π^{1/e}) totally ramified of degree e, of the hypersurface t(∑X_i^N) = N∏X_i, with an H_0-action compatible with that on the generic fibre; 𝒴 is projective. More precisely there is an H_0-equivariant projective blowup Z of US^{de}(∑X_i^N) = N∏X_i over W[S, U^{±1}]′, an isomorphism outside S = 0, étale locally étale over W[U^{±1}, S, Z_1, …, Z_m]/(US − Z_1⋯Z_r) with some Z_i inverted, and 𝒴 is its base change along S ↦ π^{1/e}, U ↦ u. Only semistability over F′ (not over F) is asserted.
hypotheses: p ∤ N
v(t) > 0 (reciprocal parameter), i.e. the Dwork parameter has negative valuation
proofSteps: Base change the model of DM.8/dwork-semistable-blowup along T ↦ S^{de}; it becomes toroidal (log smooth) but not semistable.

Subdivide the slice S = 1 of its conical complex into unimodular lattice simplices (equivariant toroidal semistable reduction, Kempf–Knudsen–Mumford–Saint-Donat, owned by SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.4); the corresponding blowup is H_0-equivariant and semistable after the ramified base change of degree e.
A blowup of a projective scheme is projective.
acceptance: d = 1 needs no subdivision: the model of DM.8/dwork-semistable-blowup is already semistable over O_F (e = 1).

sources.locator: Theorem 1.4 and Proposition 1.5, p. 3; restated as Theorem 2.3, p. 9; proof pp. 8–13 (arXiv v1)
sources.match: For v(t) = d > 0 there is a totally ramified F′ = F(π^{1/e}) and an H_0-equivariant semistable model of the fibre over O_{F′}, obtained by a toroidal subdivision.

nodes.title: The log special fibre of the semistable model lifts over W[T]
nodes.statement: In the setting of DM.8/equivariant-semistable-model, give Z the log structure M of the divisor (S) and 𝒴 that of (π^{1/e}). Choose u′ ∈ W^× with the same reduction as u and let (Y, N) be the base change of (Z, M) along S ↦ T, U ↦ u′ over Spec W[T]′ ((T^{de}u′)^N ≠ 1). Then (a) the log special fibre (𝒴̄, 𝒩̄) over (k, ℕ, 1 ↦ 0) is isomorphic, H_0-equivariantly, to the fibre of (Y, N) at T = 0; (b) Y is a projective H_0-equivariant blowup of u′T^{de}(∑X_i^N) = N∏X_i over W[T]′; (c) (Y, N) is log smooth over (W[T]′, ℕ, 1 ↦ T).
hypotheses: as in DM.8/equivariant-semistable-model
proofSteps: Both log special fibres are base changes of (Z, M) along S ↦ 0, U ↦ ū.
The charts of Z with U ↦ u′ give Kato charts of the form u′T = Z_1⋯Z_r, hence log smoothness (ComplexComparisonPartII C5 / CrystallineCohomology CR.5 log smoothness).
acceptance: For d = 1, e = 1 the lift is the reciprocal family itself near T = 0 with its semistable blowup.

sources.match: Identifies the log special fibre of the semistable model with the special fibre of a log smooth family over W[T] with log structure 1 ↦ T.

nodes.title: Hyodo–Kato description of D_st of Dwork fibres near infinity
nodes.statement: Let F/ℚ_p be finite containing ζ_N, p odd, p ∤ N, F^0 = W(k)[1/p], λ | p a prime of O, E = \overline{ℚ(ζ_N)_λ}, t ∈ F with v(t) = d > 0, and e, F′, 𝒴 as in DM.8/equivariant-semistable-model. Then V_{λ,t^{−1}}|_{G_{F′}} is semistable and for every embedding σ : F^0 ↪ E, D_st,σ(V_{λ,t^{−1}}) = ((V_{λ,t^{−1}} ⊗ E) ⊗_{σ,F^0} B_st)^{G_{F′}} ≅ (H^{N−2}_{HK}(𝒴̄, 𝒩̄))^{H_0 = σ^{−1}∘χ} ⊗_{F^0,σ} E, compatibly with φ, N and (after the B_st → B_dR comparison) the filtration. Hence V_{λ,t^{−1}} is potentially semistable, semistable over F′ (PAPER-QIAN-23/E35: not over F in general).
hypotheses: p odd, p ∤ N
v(t) > 0 (Dwork parameter t^{−1} near ∞)
proofSteps: The C_st comparison for proper semistable models (CohomologyComparisons CP.4, with the actual Hyodo–Kato complex of CrystallineCohomology CR.6) is H_0-equivariant; take σ^{−1}∘χ-eigenparts.
The Hyodo–Kato cohomology of (𝒴̄, 𝒩̄) is that of the fibre at T = 0 of the log smooth lift (DM.8/log-special-fibre-witt-lift), which computes N as the residue of the Gauss–Manin connection.
acceptance: For the self-dual data with n = 2, N on D_st is nonzero, matching a multiplicative (Tate-curve-like) degeneration.

sources.locator: §4, definition of D_st,σ (foot of p. 20) and the first display on p. 21 (arXiv v1)
sources.match: Applies Tsuji's comparison to the semistable model to identify D_st,σ of the Dwork eigenpart with the σ^{−1}χ-part of Hyodo–Kato cohomology of the log special fibre.

nodes.title: Regular ordinarity of Dwork fibres near infinity
nodes.statement: Let λ be a prime of O (of O^+ when n = 2) of odd residue characteristic l ∤ N, F_v/ℚ_l finite containing ζ_N, Qian's datum (or the self-dual datum), and t ∈ F_v with v(t) < 0. Then: (1) there is a finite totally ramified F′_v/F_v with V_{λ,t}|_{G_{F′_v}} semistable, and for every σ the monodromy operator N on D_st,σ is maximally nilpotent (N^{n−1} ≠ 0); (2) V_{λ,t} is ordinary of regular weight μ with μ_{σ,i} = M(a_σ) for all i (PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.0); (3) ordinarity with the induced weights passes to G_{F_v}-stable subquotients, and hence for a G_F-stable filtration of a global V_{λ,t} (t ∈ F) each graded piece, and the semisimplification, is ordinary at v with Hodge–Tate weights the corresponding subset of {M(a_σ), …, M(a_σ) + n − 1}. Part (2) needs the consecutive labelled weights (the companion's Lemma 4.2 omits this hypothesis of BLGHT11 Lemma 2.2(2); PAPER-QIAN-23/E11).
hypotheses: l odd, l ∤ N
proofSteps: (1): DM.8/hyodo-kato-description-near-infinity gives semistability over F′_v and identifies N with the Hyodo–Kato monodromy of the σ^{−1}χ-part; maximal nilpotence follows from maximal unipotence of the complex monodromy at ∞ for the conjugate character σ^{−1}χ (DM.4/maximal-unipotent-monodromy-at-infinity) through the comparison of the Hyodo–Kato monodromy with the residue of the Gauss–Manin connection.

(2): a semistable representation whose N is maximally nilpotent at every embedding and whose labelled Hodge–Tate weights are n consecutive integers (DM.7/dwork-hodge-tate-weights) is ordinary: weak admissibility forces the Frobenius slopes along the N-chain to be the Hodge numbers (BLGHT11 Lemma 2.2(2), in its potentially semistable form).

(3): restricting the invariant full flag to a subrepresentation (or pushing it to a quotient) gives a full flag with a subset of the graded characters, whose weights remain strictly ordered; potential semistability passes to subquotients.
acceptance: For the self-dual datum with n = 2 and v(t) < 0, V_{λ,t}((N − 3)/2) is an extension of ε^{−1}·(unramified) by an unramified character after a finite extension, like a Tate curve.

sources.match: Records that for v(t) < 0, V_{λ,t} is (potentially) semistable with maximally nilpotent monodromy and ordinary of weight (M(a_σ)), as a consequence of the companion's proof; not needed for Theorems 1.1 and 1.4.

sources.locator: Theorem 1.1, p. 2, proved in §4, pp. 19–23 (arXiv v1)
sources.match: Under maximal unipotent monodromy at ∞ for every σχ, the fibres near ∞ are ordinary of some regular weight; the printed proof uses Lemma 4.2 without the Hodge–Tate hypothesis (E11).

sources.locator: Lemma 2.2(2), as recalled in QIAN23 Lemma 2.4
sources.match: A crystalline (or semistable) representation with consecutive Hodge–Tate weights and suitable Frobenius slopes is ordinary.

nodes.title: Regular ordinarity of Dwork motives near infinity for a general character
nodes.statement: Let F/ℚ_p be finite containing ζ_N, p odd, p ∤ N, and χ(ξ) = ∏ξ_i^{a_i} an arbitrary character of H_0 (∑a_i ≡ 0) with V_λ = e_χR^{N−2}π_*O_λ of rank n. Assume (a) for every σ ∈ Gal(ℚ(ζ_N)/ℚ) the monodromy of the σχ-eigen-local-system at t = ∞ has minimal polynomial (X − 1)^n, and (b) for every embedding the labelled Hodge–Tate weights of V_{λ,t^{−1}} are n consecutive integers. Then for every finite F_0/F and t ∈ F_0 with v(t) > 0, V_{λ,t^{−1}} is ordinary of some regular weight. Hypothesis (a) for all σ follows from the case σ = 1 by coefficient conjugation. The companion's sufficient condition 'a zero exponent gives (a)' is false (PAPER-QIAN-23/E50), and hypothesis (b) is not established for general χ there (E11).
hypotheses: (a) maximal unipotent monodromy at ∞ for every Galois conjugate σχ
(b) consecutive labelled Hodge–Tate weights
proofSteps: As in DM.8/ordinary-near-infinity, using DM.8/hyodo-kato-description-near-infinity for χ and hypotheses (a), (b) in place of the computations for Qian's datum.
acceptance: For Qian's datum, (a) is DM.4/maximal-unipotent-monodromy-at-infinity and (b) is DM.7/dwork-hodge-tate-weights, recovering DM.8/ordinary-near-infinity.

sources.locator: Theorem 1.1 and Remark 1.2, p. 2; §4, pp. 19–23 (arXiv v1)
sources.match: The conditional main theorem of the companion, with the hypothesis of maximal unipotent monodromy for every σχ; Remark 1.2's zero-exponent criterion is false (E50).

nodes.title: Determinant twists, the module W and the torsor T_W for Qian's switch
nodes.statement: Hypotheses: l odd, n = l^a m (l ∤ m), s ≥ 1, N odd prime to ln with N > 100n + 100, r the order of l mod N with N ∤ l^{r/2} + 1 if r is even; F a CM field, M = F(ζ_N); r̄ : G_F → GL_n(𝔽_{l^s}) continuous; λ | l a prime of O (of O^+ when n = 2) with k(λ) ⊇ 𝔽_{l²} and all m-th roots of elements of 𝔽_{l^s}; l′ > 2ln + 5 prime, unramified in F^avoid, l′ ≡ 1 mod N and l′ ≡ 1 mod n (PAPER-QIAN-23/E7, E36); λ′ | l′, k(λ′) = 𝔽_{l′}; r̄′ : G_F → GL_n(𝔽_{l′}) with det r̄′ = ε̄_{l′}^{−n(n−1)/2} (E9); finite Galois F^avoid ⊇ F, F_2^avoid, and totally real Galois F^suff over ℚ, all unramified above N, with F_2^avoid ∩ F^avoid = ℚ and F^suff ∩ F^avoid F_2^avoid = ℚ; F_0 = F^avoid F_2^avoid F^suff(ζ_N). Construction: apply ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4 (roots after totally real base change) to det V[λ] ⊗ (det r̄|_{G_M})^{−1} (exponent m, DM.6/determinant-matching-at-l) avoiding F_0, getting L_1; then over L_1M to (det r̄′)^{−1} ⊗ det V[λ′] (exponent n, DM.6/determinant-matching-at-auxiliary-prime) avoiding F_0L_1, getting L_2 (two applications with the enlarged avoidance field, E37). Put L = L_1L_2, E = LM. This gives (a) a totally real Galois L/ℚ linearly disjoint from F_0 and the CM field E, Galois over F; (b) characters χ̄_1 : G_E → k(λ)^×, χ̄_2 : G_E → 𝔽_{l′}^× with χ̄_1^n = det V[λ] ⊗ (det r̄)^{−1} and χ̄_2^n = det V[λ′] ⊗ (det r̄′)^{−1}; (c) W = (χ̄_1 ⊗ r̄) × (χ̄_2 ⊗ r̄′) over O/λλ′ ≅ k(λ) × 𝔽_{l′} with det W ≅ det V[λλ′], hence φ : ∧^nW ≅ ∧^nV[λλ′] and the torsor T_W = T({W}) over (T_0)_E (DM.5/level-structure-torsor); (d) T_W is smooth and geometrically irreducible (DM.5/level-structure-torsor-irreducible: l ≠ l′, max(l, l′) > 10, r′ = 1); (e) E ∩ F^avoid F_2^avoid F^suff = F.
hypotheses: all hypotheses listed in the statement
proofSteps: The two root extractions are DM.6/determinant-matching-at-l and DM.6/determinant-matching-at-auxiliary-prime combined with the AGD R02.4 root theorem; the second application must avoid F_0L_1 so that L = L_1L_2 stays disjoint from F_0 (E37).
Then det(χ̄_1 ⊗ r̄) = det V[λ] and det(χ̄_2 ⊗ r̄′) = det V[λ′], which gives φ by DM.5/determinant-descends.

(e): L and F_0 are linearly disjoint and M ⊂ F_0, so E ∩ F_0 = M; F^avoid F_2^avoid F^suff is unramified above N, hence meets ℚ(ζ_N) in ℚ, so M ∩ F^avoid F_2^avoid F^suff = F (tower disjointness, PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R23.1).
acceptance: When r̄ already has determinant det V[λ]|_{G_F} and r̄′ has determinant det V[λ′], one may take L = ℚ and χ̄_1 = χ̄_2 = 1.

sources.locator: §4, application of Lemma 2.1 and construction of W and φ, pp. 1270–1271
sources.match: Constructs E = LM, the characters χ_1, χ_2, the module W and the isomorphism φ, and observes T_W is geometrically connected by Proposition 3.8, with the corrections E5–E7, E9, E36, E37.

the switching point feeds Qian's Theorems 1.1 and 1.4

nodes.title: Weil restriction of the torsor and the local valuation conditions
nodes.statement: With the switching data of DM.9/switching-determinant-data, let T = Res_{EF^suff/ℚ}(T_W ×_E EF^suff), a smooth geometrically irreducible ℚ-variety (Weil restriction along a finite separable extension preserves both properties), with the morphism p : T → Res_{EF^suff/ℚ} T_0 induced by T_W → (T_0)_E. Put Ω_∞ = T(ℝ) (nonempty since EF^suff is CM: T(ℝ) = ∏_{complex places} T_W(ℂ)), Ω_{l,0} = {(t_τ) : v_l(t_τ) < 0 for all τ : EF^suff → ℚ̄_l}, Ω_{l′,0} = {(t_τ) : v_{l′}(t_τ) > 0 for all τ}, and Ω_l = p^{−1}(Ω_{l,0}), Ω_{l′} = p^{−1}(Ω_{l′,0}). These are nonempty open subsets, invariant under Gal(ℚ̄_l/ℚ_l) (resp. Gal(ℚ̄_{l′}/ℚ_{l′})).
hypotheses: EF^suff a CM field
T_W smooth geometrically irreducible
proofSteps: Weil restriction of a quasi-projective smooth variety along a finite separable extension is a smooth quasi-projective variety, and becomes a product of conjugates over ℚ̄, hence geometrically irreducible (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.3; AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A6).
t with v(t) < 0 (resp. > 0) avoids μ_N and ∞, so Ω_{l,0}, Ω_{l′,0} are nonempty open Galois-stable; p is finite étale and surjective on ℚ̄_l-points, so the preimages are nonempty open.
acceptance: If EF^suff has degree 2d over ℚ, then T(ℝ) is the product of d copies of T_W(ℂ), one for each complex place.

sources.match: Applies Moret-Bailly to T = Res_{EF^suff/ℚ}T_W with Ω_∞ = T(ℝ) and the opens Ω_l, Ω_{l′} defined by v_l(t_τ) < 0, v_{l′}(t_τ) > 0.

nodes.title: Qian's switching theorem for non-self-dual Dwork motives
nodes.statement: Keep the switching data of DM.9/switching-determinant-data. There are a finite totally real Galois L′/ℚ, linearly disjoint from F_0L over ℚ, and, with F′ = L′EF^suff, a point t ∈ T_0(F′) with a G_{F′}-equivariant isomorphism W ≅ V[λλ′]_t inducing φ_t on ∧^n, such that: (i) F′ ⊇ EF^suff is CM, finite Galois over F, with (F′)^+ = L′E^+F^suff; (ii) χ̄_1^{−1}V[λ]_t ≅ r̄|_{G_{F′}} and χ̄_2^{−1}V[λ′]_t ≅ r̄′|_{G_{F′}}; (iii) v(t) < 0 for every place v | l of F′ and v(t) > 0 for every v | l′; (iv) F′ ∩ F_2^avoid = ℚ and F′ ∩ F^avoid F_2^avoid = F, so F′ is linearly disjoint over F from every subextension of F^avoid F_2^avoid (in Qian's §4 these include F^av and F̄^{ker r̄}); (v) K = L′LF^suff(ζ_N) is finite Galois over ℚ with FK = F′ and K ∩ F^avoid = ℚ (the field that must be disjoint from F^avoid in the proof of Theorem 1.4; PAPER-QIAN-23/E3). Consequently V_{λ,t} has the prescribed residual representation at l, V_{λ′,t} at l′, V_{λ′,t} is ordinary at the places above l′ (DM.7/ordinary-near-fermat-point), and V_{λ′,t} has maximal unipotent (Steinberg-type) monodromy at the places above l (DM.7/steinberg-monodromy-away-from-coefficient-prime). No automorphy statement is made here.
hypotheses: the hypotheses of DM.9/switching-determinant-data
proofSteps: Apply Moret-Bailly with three kinds of local conditions (PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R23.1) over ℚ to T = Res_{EF^suff/ℚ}T_W with S_1 = {∞}, S_2 = ∅, S_3 = {l, l′}, the opens of DM.9/weil-restricted-local-conditions and H = F_0L; ℚ is totally real with its real place in S_1, so the extension L′ is totally real.

A point of T over L′ is a point of T_W over L′EF^suff = F′ (L′ and EF^suff linearly disjoint), i.e. t ∈ T_0(F′) with an isomorphism W ≅ V[λλ′]_t respecting φ: this gives (ii) after untwisting by χ̄_i, and (iii) from the local conditions.
(iv) and (v) are intersection computations with tower disjointness (R23.1), using that L′ is disjoint from F_0L, L from F_0, and F^avoid F_2^avoid F^suff from ℚ(ζ_N).
The local consequences at l′ and l are DM.7/ordinary-near-fermat-point (l′ ≡ 1 mod N, v(t) > 0 means t ∈ 𝔪) and DM.7/steinberg-monodromy-away-from-coefficient-prime (l′ ≠ l, v(t) < 0).
acceptance: For n = 2 the theorem reduces to the self-dual switch of BLGHT11 §6 with the real coefficient field, and its residual representations are symplectic.

sources.locator: §4, outcome of Proposition 4.2 and the intersection computations, p. 1272; proof of Theorem 1.4, p. 1274 (E3)
sources.match: Produces L′, F′ and t ∈ T_0(F′) with χ_1^{−1}V[λ]_t ≅ r̄|G_{F′}, χ_2^{−1}V[λ′]_t ≅ Sym^{n−1}r̄_{E,l′}|G_{F′}, v(t) < 0 above l and > 0 above l′, and the disjointness properties.

nodes.title: Switching in the self-dual Dwork family
nodes.statement: Let F/F_0 be a finite Galois extension of totally real fields, I a finite set, and for i ∈ I: n_i even, l_i odd primes, r̄_i : G_F → GSp_{n_i}(𝔽̄_{l_i}) with open kernel and multiplier ε̄_{l_i}^{1−n_i}; let l′ be a prime and r̄′_i : G_F → GSp_{n_i}(𝔽_{l′}) with multiplier ε̄_{l′}^{1−n_i}, and F^avoid/F finite Galois. Choose N odd, prime to 2∏l_i·l′, N > n_i + 1, divisible by no prime ramified in F^avoid, such that each r̄_i takes values in GSp_{n_i}(Z[ζ_N]^+/λ_i) for a prime λ_i | l_i of ℤ[ζ_N]^+ (DM.1/auxiliary-modulus, BLGHT11 Lemma 6.1), and λ′ | l′. Then the product over i of the symplectic level-structure torsors T_{r̄_i × r̄′_i} over T_0 × Spec F(ζ_N)^+ (isomorphisms compatible with the symplectic structures, BLGGT14's correction) is geometrically irreducible, and for any finite Galois L/F(ζ_N)^+ disjoint from it and any finite set Σ of places, Moret-Bailly gives a totally real F′/F_0 Galois, linearly disjoint from F^avoid over F, and t_i ∈ T_0(F′) with: V_{n_i}[λ_i]((N − 1 − n_i)/2)_{t_i} ≅ r̄_i|_{G_{F′}} and V_{n_i}[λ′]((N − 1 − n_i)/2)_{t_i} ≅ r̄′_i|_{G_{F′}} as symplectic representations; v(t_i) < 0 at every place above l_i (and, in the variant of Newton–Thorne and Fakhruddin–Khare–Patrikis, above Σ), v(t_i) > 0 at every place above l′. At such points: V_{λ′,t_i} is ordinary of weight 0 at the places above l′ (when l′ ≡ 1 mod N), has Hodge–Tate numbers {0, …, n_i − 1}, and at places above l_i (and Σ) the Weil–Deligne representation of V_{λ′,t_i} is an unramified twist of Steinberg.
hypotheses: n_i even; multipliers ε̄^{1−n_i}
N chosen as above; l′ ≡ 1 mod N for the ordinarity at l′
proofSteps: Construct the self-dual real forms and their symplectic torsors (DM.2/self-dual-real-forms, DM.5/level-structure-torsor); geometric irreducibility of the product follows from the full symplectic monodromy at each prime and DM.5/two-prime-product-monodromy (BLGHT11 Proposition 4.2).

Apply Moret-Bailly over a preliminary extension (PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R23.1, the corrected BLGHT11 Proposition 6.2 and BLGGT14 Proposition 3.1.1) with the local opens v(t) < 0 above l_i and Σ, v(t) > 0 above l′.
Local properties: DM.7/ordinary-near-fermat-point at l′, DM.7/dwork-hodge-tate-weights, DM.7/steinberg-monodromy-away-from-coefficient-prime at l_i and Σ.
acceptance: n_i = 2: the residual representations are GL_2 = GSp_2-valued with determinant ε̄^{−1}, and the switch produces a fibre that is Steinberg above l_i, the shape used by BLGGT14 Theorem 3.1.2.

sources.match: Chooses N by BLGHT11 Lemma 6.1, constructs the sheaves V_{n_i,λ_i}((N − 1 − n_i)/2) and the covers T_{r̄_i × r̄′_i} of BLGHT11 §4 (with isomorphisms respecting the symplectic structures), and finds a point by Proposition 3.1.1 with v(t) < 0 above l_i and v(t) > 0 above l′.
The self-dual Dwork family, its symplectic monodromy, local Galois properties of its fibres and the Moret-Bailly variant used to find points.
Uses the self-dual family for n = 2.

nodes.title: Local constancy of Galois representations in the Dwork family (Kisin)
nodes.statement: Let v | l be a place of a number field F ⊇ ℚ(ζ_N), λ | l a place of M, t ∈ T_0(O_{F_v}) and c > 0. There is an open ball U_t ∋ t in T_0(O_{F_v}) such that for all t′ ∈ U_t, W_{t,λ}/l^c ≅ W_{t′,λ}/l^c as representations of G_{F_v} (and likewise for finitely many λ simultaneously).
hypotheses: t integral with good reduction
proofSteps: Kisin's local constancy theorem for p-adic families: for a smooth proper family over a p-adic disc, the Galois representations on the cohomology of nearby fibres are congruent modulo any fixed power of p on a small enough disc (a Krasner-type lemma for families).
Apply it to e_χ R^{N−2}π_* and twist by Ψ_λ^{−1}.
acceptance: If t ≡ t′ modulo a high power of the uniformiser, the reductions W̄_{t,λ} and W̄_{t′,λ} are isomorphic.

sources.match: Uses Kisin's local constancy theorem to find open balls on which W_{t,λ} mod p^c is constant.
Local constancy in p-adic families of Galois representations.

nodes.title: Reductions of two-dimensional crystalline representations of small weight (Berger)
nodes.statement: Let p be an odd prime and r : G_{ℚ_p} → GL_2(ℚ̄_p) crystalline with Hodge–Tate weights {0, m}, 1 ≤ m ≤ p − 1. Then either r is ordinary, or r̄|_{G_{ℚ_{p²}}} is isomorphic to an unramified twist of ρ̄_{2,m,0} = ε̄_2^{m} ⊕ (ε̄′_2)^{m} (the restriction of the induction of the m-th power of a fundamental character of level two).
proofSteps: Fontaine–Laffaille theory (or the explicit reduction of V_{k,a_p}) classifies the crystalline lattices in this range; v_p(a_p) = 0 gives the ordinary case, v_p(a_p) > 0 gives the irreducible induced reduction.
acceptance: A supersingular elliptic curve at p (m = 1): r̄|_{I_p} ≅ ω_2 ⊕ ω_2^p, the non-ordinary branch.

sources.match: Splits the p-adic places into Σ^ord and Σ^ss using Berger's reduction theorem.
Reduction of two-dimensional crystalline representations with Hodge–Tate weights {0, m}, m ≤ p − 1.

nodes.title: Local Dwork points with prescribed reductions (Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Newton–Thorne)
nodes.statement: In the setting of the proof of BCGNT25 Theorem 6.2.4 (primes p ≡ −1 mod N, r ≡ 1 mod N, p_0, q, places 𝔭, 𝔯, 𝔮 of M above p, r, q, a CM field F_4 = K^+F_3 with K^+_v large and the residual representations r̄_𝔭, r̄_𝔯, r̄_{CM,𝔯}, ρ̄_{A,q} trivial on G_{F_{4,v}} for v | prp_0q), for k ∈ {m, nm} and each such v there is a nonempty open _kΩ_v ⊂ T_0(O_{F_{4,v}}) of points t with: (i) v ∈ Σ^ord: _kW̄_{t,𝔭} trivial, _kW_{t,𝔭} crystalline ordinary, _kW̄_{t,𝔯}, _kW̄_{t,𝔮} trivial; (ii) v ∈ Σ^ss: _kW_{t,𝔭} crystalline and connected to ρ_{k,1,0} (the Fontaine–Laffaille representation ⊕ε_2^{k−i}(ε′_2)^{i−1}), residuals trivial; (iii) v | r: _kW_{t,𝔯} crystalline ordinary, residuals trivial; (iv) v | p_0: all residuals trivial; (v) v | q: _kW_{t,𝔮} crystalline ordinary, residuals trivial. Here _kW denotes the twisted Dwork system of rank k.
hypotheses: p > nm with p ≡ −1 mod N; r, q ≡ 1 or split as specified; F_4 chosen so residual representations are trivial locally
proofSteps: (i), (iii), (v): DM.7/generic-crystalline-ordinarity gives an ordinary crystalline point; Kisin's local constancy (DM.9/kisin-local-constancy) and the component lemmas for weight-zero crystalline lifts (LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7, BCGNT25 Lemmas 5.1.4–5.1.5) give an open ball of such points with trivial residual representations after enlarging F_4.

(ii): at t = 0, W_{0,𝔭} restricted to inertia is ⊕ω_τ^{i−1}ω_{cτ}^{k−i} (DM.7/fermat-fibre-inertia-at-minus-one), so its crystalline lifts connect to ρ_{k,1,0} (BCGNT25 Lemma 5.1.3, LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7); local constancy gives an open neighbourhood.
(iv): any point with trivial residual representations near t = 0 after enlarging F_4.
acceptance: For k = m = 2 the ordinary points of (i) correspond to ordinary crystalline rank-two representations with Hodge–Tate weights {0, 1}.

nodes.title: The CM-induced auxiliary system R_CM
nodes.statement: In the proof of BCGNT25 Theorem 6.2.4: let F_1 be the Galois closure of FF_0, E/ℚ totally real cyclic of degree m disjoint from F_1 with p_0 unramified, L_1 = EF_1, q_1 an odd prime splitting completely in L_1 with v_1 | q_1 split as w_1⋯w_m in L_1. Choose an algebraic Hecke character Ψ_0 : 𝔸_{L_1}^× → M^× of the infinity type of Proposition 6.2.3(6a), unramified above the relevant set, with the restrictions Ψ_0|_{O^×_{L_{1,w_i}}} wildly ramified, pairwise distinct and of product 1; then (ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4, BCGNT25 Lemma 5.3.3) a CM F_2/F_1 and a finite-order twist Ψ_2 of Ψ_0 ∘ N_{L_2/L_1} with det Ind Ψ_{2,λ} = ε^{−m(m−1)/2}. Then R_CM = {Ind_{G_{L_2}}^{G_{F_2}} Ψ_{2,λ}}_λ is a weakly compatible system of rank m, with Hodge–Tate weights {0, …, m − 1} and residual representations r̄_{CM,λ} absolutely irreducible on G_{F_2(ζ_N, ζ_r)} for the chosen r.
hypotheses: the infinity type of BCGNT25 Proposition 6.2.3(6a)
proofSteps: Existence of Ψ_0 with prescribed infinity type and local restrictions: algebraic Hecke characters with prescribed restrictions to finitely many local unit groups (HSBT10 Lemma 2.2 as restated in BLGGT14 Lemma A.2.4; PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.0).
The determinant correction by a finite-order twist after a CM base change is a root extraction of a finite-order character (ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4).

Induction of a compatible system of characters is a compatible system (PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R24.5); distinctness of the local restrictions at w_i gives irreducibility of the residual induction.
acceptance: m = 1: R_CM is the character system of Ψ_2 itself.

sources.locator: Proof of Theorem 6.2.4, construction of Ψ and R_CM, published pp. 57–58 (arXiv v3 pp. 64–65)
sources.match: Constructs Ψ_0 by HSBT10 Lemma 2.2, the CM extension F_2 and the twist Ψ_2 by Lemma 5.3.3, and R_CM = {Ind Ψ_{2,λ}}.

nodes.title: Choice of primes and fields for the p–r switch
nodes.statement: Given R (the rank-two compatible system of BCGNT25 Theorem 6.2.4 over F_2, with its set of good primes L(R)) and R_CM, there are primes N, p, r, q and fields with: N > 100nm + 100 prime, unramified in L_2 and M; p ≡ −1 mod N, r ≡ 1 mod N; p, r > 2nm + 1, p, r ∈ L(R|_{G_{F_2}}) prime to v_0v_1; p split in L_2 and M, r split in L_2(ζ_p) and M; Ψ_2 unramified above p and r; r̄_𝔭, r̄_𝔯 with image between SL_2 and GL_2; r̄_{CM,𝔯}|_{G_{F_2(ζ_N, ζ_r)}} absolutely irreducible; the p-adic places split into Σ^ord ∪ Σ^ss by DM.9/berger-reduction-small-weight; a solvable CM F_3/F_2(ζ_N) disjoint from the field B cut out by r̄_𝔭 × r̄_𝔯 × r̄_{CM,𝔯}; and, after adjoining e^{2πi/N} to M, a semistable elliptic curve A/ℚ with good reduction at p, r, p_0 and a prime q ∉ {p, r, p_0}, q > 2nm + 1, split in M, with ρ̄_{A,q}(G_{F_3}) = GL_2(𝔽_q) and A good ordinary at q.
hypotheses: the hypotheses of BCGNT25 Theorem 6.2.4
proofSteps: Primes p ≡ −1, r ≡ 1 mod N with the splitting conditions have positive density (Chebotarev); the excluded sets are finite or of density zero (big image for R at almost all primes).
Berger's theorem sorts the places above p.

A semistable non-CM elliptic curve over ℚ has surjective mod-q image for almost all q and is ordinary at a density-one set of primes (Serre); choose q accordingly, avoiding p, r, p_0 (as corrected in the extraction's review).
acceptance: p = 2N − 1 and r = 2N + 1 satisfy the congruences when they are prime.

nodes.title: The auxiliary Dwork systems R_aux and S_UA (Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Newton–Thorne)
nodes.statement: Let m > 2 and keep the data of DM.9/bcgnt-switching-primes and DM.9/bcgnt-local-dwork-points. (1) Applying Moret-Bailly with surjective specialisation (PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R23.1) to T(r̄_{CM,𝔯}|_{G_{F_4}}) (r ≡ 1 mod N, DM.5/level-structure-torsor), with f : π_1^ét(T) ↠ G the surjection onto the image G ⊆ GU_m(𝔽_{p²}) of the residual system W̄_𝔭 (G ⊇ SU_m(𝔽_{p²}), DM.5/residual-monodromy-su), F^avoid = B′F_4, S_0 = {p, r, p_0, q} and the opens _mΩ_v, gives a CM F_5 and t with R_aux = {W_{t,λ}}: r̄_{aux,𝔭}(G_{F_5}) = G with multiplier ε̄^{1−m}, r̄_{aux,𝔭}(G_{F_5(ζ_p)}) = SU_m(𝔽_{p²}), r̄_{aux,𝔯} ≅ r̄_{CM,𝔯}, and the local properties (i)–(v). (2) Applying it again to T(s̄_{aux,𝔭}, Sym^{nm−1}ρ̄_{A,q}|_{G_{F_5}}) for the rank-nm Dwork system, with F^avoid enlarged by the field cut out by r̄_{aux,𝔭}, gives F_6 and S_UA with s̄_{UA,𝔭} ≅ s̄_{aux,𝔭}, s̄_{UA,𝔮} ≅ Sym^{nm−1}ρ̄_{A,q} and the local properties (Hermitian structures being unique over finite fields). The printed claims r̄_{aux,𝔭}(G_{F_5}) = GU_m(𝔽_{p²}) and F^avoid = B′F_5 are corrected as PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25/E29 and E32.
hypotheses: m > 2 (for m = 2 see DM.9/rank-two-auxiliary-system)
η compatible with the Hermitian pairings (E23)
proofSteps: The torsors are smooth and geometrically irreducible (DM.5/level-structure-torsor-irreducible); the opens are nonempty (DM.9/bcgnt-local-dwork-points); the map f to the residual monodromy image is surjective on π_1^ét because the geometric monodromy is already SU_m.
Moret-Bailly with surjective specialisation yields F_5 and a point whose residual image is all of G, and its intersection with G_{F_5(ζ_p)} is SU_m (the multiplier ε̄^{1−m} cuts it out).
The second application uses DM.0/hermitian-forms-unique to match the Hermitian structure of s̄_{aux,𝔭} with that of the rank-nm Dwork system.
acceptance: det r_aux = ε^{−m(m−1)/2} is compatible with the image G but not with GU_m(𝔽_{p²}) in full, which is why the printed equality is corrected.

nodes.title: The auxiliary system R_aux in rank two via twisted modular curves
nodes.statement: Let m = 2 in the setting of DM.9/bcgnt-auxiliary-dwork-systems. There are a CM field F_5/F_4, disjoint from B′F_4, and an elliptic curve A_aux/F_5 such that R_aux = {H¹(A_aux)_λ} satisfies: ρ̄_{A_aux,r} ≅ r̄_{CM,𝔯}|_{G_{F_5}} (symplectically); ρ̄_{A_aux,p}(G_{F_5(ζ_p)}) = SL_2(𝔽_p) = SU_2(𝔽_{p²}) up to the identification of SU_2 with SL_2; at v ∈ Σ^ss, ρ_{A_aux,p}|G_{F_{5,v}} connects to ρ_{2,1,0} (A_aux supersingular), at Σ^ord ordinary, at v | r ordinary, and the residual representations are trivial locally as in (i)–(v). The source omits this case ('a straightforward variant, left to the reader').
proofSteps: The twisted modular curve Y(r̄) parametrising elliptic curves A with a symplectic isomorphism A[r] ≅ r̄_{CM,𝔯} is a smooth geometrically connected fine moduli curve (Tau Ceti ModularCurves, layer 5C).

The local opens: at v ∈ Σ^ss, curves with supersingular good reduction whose p-torsion is the level-two induced representation (an open condition in the p-adic topology near a supersingular CM point); at Σ^ord and v | r, ordinary good reduction with trivial residual representations after the local enlargement; at p_0, q, trivial residuals.
Moret-Bailly with surjective specialisation (R23.1), with f the mod-p monodromy of the universal curve, whose geometric image is SL_2(𝔽_p).
acceptance: For m = 2, SU_2(𝔽_{p²}) ≅ SL_2(𝔽_p), so the image requirement is the familiar surjectivity onto SL_2(𝔽_p).

sources.match: For m = 2 the auxiliary system is built from a modular curve with level-r structure instead of the Dwork family, and the details are left to the reader.

requests.need: Henniart's theorem: a family of λ-adic characters of G_K, for all places λ of a number field M, with Frobenius values in M independent of λ at almost all places, is attached to an algebraic Hecke character of K of type A_0 with values in M.

Compactly supported direct image Rf_!, external products and the Künneth formula for constructible ℓ-adic complexes, so that multiplicative convolution A ∗_! B = Rm_!(A ⊠ B) on 𝔾_m over ℤ[1/ℓ]-schemes is defined, associative and compatible with base change and with the trace formula.

BCGNT25 Lemmas 5.1.3–5.1.5 for weight-0 crystalline lifts over unramified-at-p fields with p > nm: crystalline lifts of ρ̄_{n,m,0} connect to ρ_{n,m,0} after any finite extension; ordinary weight-0 crystalline lifts of the trivial representation connect; sufficiently p-adically close weight-0 crystalline lifts lie on the same component.

Étale cohomology of schemes with ℤ/ℓ^k, ℤ_ℓ and ℚ_ℓ coefficients, ℓ invertible: (a) smooth and proper base change, so that R^iπ_* of a smooth proper morphism is lisse, commutes with base change and has stalks the cohomology of geometric fibres; (b) the Artin comparison between étale cohomology with finite coefficients of a complex variety and singular cohomology, in the relative form for R^iπ_* of a smooth proper morphism over a complex base; (c) the equivalence between lisse sheaves on a connected scheme and continuous representations of its étale fundamental group, with the homotopy exact sequence π_1^geom → π_1 → G_K; (d) the Grothendieck–Lefschetz trace formula over finite fields; (e) cup product, trace and Poincaré duality for smooth proper varieties, compatible with finite group actions.

Equivariant toroidal semistable reduction (Kempf–Knudsen–Mumford–Saint-Donat): for a log smooth (toroidal) family over a complete discrete valuation ring with a finite group acting on the toroidal charts by characters, a subdivision of the conical complex into unimodular simplices gives, after a totally ramified base change of suitable degree e, an equivariant projective blowup that is strictly semistable.
π_1 of ℙ¹(ℂ) − {0, 1, ∞} is free on two peripheral loops, with the product relation among the three peripheral classes in the layer's composition convention.
The Chebotarev density theorem: Frobenius elements are dense, and primes with prescribed Frobenius conjugacy class in a finite Galois extension have positive Dirichlet density.

The twisted modular curve Y(ρ) for a Galois representation ρ on (ℤ/r)² with cyclotomic determinant, r ≥ 3: a smooth geometrically connected fine moduli curve of elliptic curves with a symplectic isomorphism of their r-torsion with ρ, with its universal elliptic curve.

gaps.title: Katz's theory of hypergeometric sheaves (ESDE Chapter 8) not read
gaps.detail: The properties of E_λ (lisse of rank n, geometric irreducibility, purity, determinant via Theorem 8.12.2(1a)) and its local monodromy at 0, 1, ∞ (Theorem 8.4.2, cited as 8.4.11 by BLGHT11) are taken in the form BCGNT25 and BLGHT11 apply them; Katz's book was not available. No atlas roadmap plans general hypergeometric sheaves (KloostermanMomentsAndPotentialAutomorphy KM.1 constructs Kloosterman sheaves directly). Closing this gap means planning the convolution theory of Katz's Chapter 8 for tame characters: rank, local monodromy and determinant of H_can(χ's; ρ's).

gaps.title: Zalesskii–Serezhkin and Artin's order theorem not read
gaps.detail: Both are used in the form stated by QIAN23 and BLGHT11. The exceptional cases of the Zalesskii–Serezhkin list (characteristic 2 and 3, small dimension) and the precise coincidences excluded by Artin's Theorem 2 must be checked against the originals; in the applications the monodromy contains an element of order N > 100n + 100 and both characteristics are odd with one > 10, which excludes every exception known to this design.

gaps.title: Kisin's local constancy and Berger's reduction theorem not read
gaps.detail: Both are cited in the form BCGNT25 applies them (Kis99 Theorem 5.1; Ber10 Théorème 3.2.1). Kisin's theorem needs its exact hypotheses on the family (smooth proper over a p-adic disc) checked; Berger's needs the range 1 ≤ m ≤ p − 1 and the twist conventions of ρ̄_{2,m,0} checked.

gaps.title: The rank-two auxiliary system of BCGNT25 Theorem 6.2.4 is not written in the source
gaps.detail: For m = 2 the paper leaves the construction from a modular curve with level-r structure to the reader. The node gives the construction through twisted modular curves and Moret-Bailly with surjective specialisation; the existence of a nonempty open set of supersingular points at v ∈ Σ^ss whose p-adic representation connects to ρ_{2,1,0}, and the surjectivity of the mod-p geometric monodromy of the universal curve over the twisted modular curve, must be proved in detail.

gaps.title: Regular ordinarity near infinity for a general character
gaps.detail: The companion preprint QIAN21 proves its main theorem through its Lemma 4.2, which omits the consecutive Hodge–Tate hypothesis of BLGHT11 Lemma 2.2(2) (PAPER-QIAN-23/E11), and its Remark 1.2 criterion is false (E50). For Qian's datum and the self-dual data both hypotheses are proved here (DM.4, DM.7), so DM.8/ordinary-near-infinity is unaffected; for a general character the consecutive-weight hypothesis remains a hypothesis. A possible route (maximal unipotence forcing consecutive Hodge numbers through the limiting mixed Hodge structure) is not in any source read.

gaps.title: Katz–Messing for twisted Frobenius and Deligne's Fermat propositions read only through citations
gaps.detail: PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology RD.7 plans the crystalline–ℓ-adic comparison of Frobenius characteristic polynomials; the version for h·Frob with h in a finite group acting (KM74 Theorem 2(2), used through the projector e_χ) is a mild extension that RD.7 should state. Deligne's Propositions I.7.4, I.7.6 and I.7.10 were located in a scanned copy without a text layer and used as BLGHT11 and QIAN23 state them.

gaps.title: Tame specialisation for fibres near infinity and crystalline companions
gaps.detail: The identification of the inertia action on a fibre at a point with v(t) < 0 with a power of the local monodromy of the family at ∞ follows Harris–Shepherd-Barron–Taylor Lemma 1.15(2) (not read) through nearby cycles (LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles LPV.0–LPV.1); the precise specialisation statement for a family over the punctured disc around ∞ should be stated there. Drinfeld–Kedlaya's transfer to lisse sheaves uses Abe's crystalline companions, which no atlas layer plans.

sourceIssues.locator: Lemma 3.12, p. 1267 (statement; proof ends p. 1268). The lemma takes its range of t from the opening of Lemma 3.11, p. 1266: "let t ∈ F_v as a point in T_0(F_v)". Its only use is in the proof of Lemma 4.3, p. 1273.
sourceIssues.printed: Lemma 3.12 takes a place λ′ of Q(ζ_N) over an odd prime l′ ≠ l not dividing N, under the preceding assumptions. Viewing V_{λ′,t} as a G_{F_v}-representation, it asserts that the N in WD(V_{λ′,t}) = (r_1, N) is maximally nilpotent.
sourceIssues.correction: Add the hypothesis v(t) < 0. The corrected statement: let v be a place of F above l, and let t ∈ F_v with v(t) < 0 (so t lies in T_0(F_v) and is v-adically close to ∞). Then the monodromy operator of WD(V_{λ′,t}|G_{F_v}) is maximally nilpotent. This is the hypothesis v_K(a) < 0 of Harris–Shepherd-Barron–Taylor, Lemma 1.15, whose argument the proof cites. It also holds wherever the lemma is used: Lemma 4.3 (p. 1273) assumes v(t) < 0 at every l-adic place. With this hypothesis the cited argument works. The restriction of V_{λ′} to the punctured formal neighbourhood of t = ∞ over W(F̄_l) is lisse, because l ∤ N. So inertia at v acts through its tame Z_{l′}-quotient by exp(v(t)·t_{l′}·N_∞), where N_∞ is the logarithm of the monodromy at ∞. That monodromy is maximally unipotent by Corollary 3.5: the loop around t = ∞ is the N-th power of the loop around t′ = ∞, and it is still a single Jordan block. A nonzero multiple of a maximally nilpotent operator in characteristic 0 is again maximally nilpotent, so the corrected statement follows.
sourceIssues.reason: As printed, the lemma covers every t ∈ T_0(F_v), because the only standing condition on t is the one from Lemma 3.11 (p. 1266). The statement is false for t = 0, and more generally for any t ∈ O_{F_v} with t^N − 1 a unit. For such t the hypersurface X_1^N + … + X_N^N = N t X_1⋯X_N has good reduction at v. At a singular point of the reduction the partial derivatives give X_i^N = t X_1⋯X_N for every i, because N is invertible (l ∤ N). Taking the product over i gives (1 − t^N)(X_1⋯X_N)^N = 0, which forces every X_i = 0. The paper uses this same good reduction in Lemma 3.11(2). Since l′ ≠ l, smooth proper base change makes H^{N−2}_et(Y_t ×F̄_v, Z[ζ_N]_{λ′}) unramified at v. Because ζ_N ∈ F, the H_0-action is defined over O_{F_v}, so the χ-eigenspace V_{λ′,t} is also unramified. Hence WD(V_{λ′,t}) has N = 0. But V_{λ′,t} has rank n ≥ 2 (Proposition 3.2, p. 1257), so by Definition 3.6 N = 0 is not maximally nilpotent: its minimal polynomial is X, not X^n. For t = 0 this is completely explicit: V_{λ′,0} is a sum of n characters on which Frobenius acts by Jacobi sums (proof of Lemma 3.9, p. 1262), all unramified at v. A direct check on small Dwork hypersurfaces (N = 3 over F_7 and F_13, N = 5 over F_11) gives singular reduction exactly when t^N ≡ 1. The proof only covers v(t) < 0. It appeals to the monodromy around ∞ and to Harris–Shepherd-Barron–Taylor Lemma 1.15(2), whose statement assumes v_K(a) < 0. Remark 3.13 (p. 1268) also reads the lemma as a statement about v(t) < 0. The recorded correction is right and sufficient. The main theorems are unaffected, because the only application, Lemma 4.3 (p. 1273), has v(t) < 0 at every l-adic place, and there l′ ≡ 1 mod N and l′ > 2ln + 5 (Proposition 4.1, p. 1269). This is an error, not a misprint: a stated lemma is false as printed, not merely mistyped. The intended hypothesis can still be recovered from the context.

sourceIssues.printed: The source claims that the normal closure of \overline{F}^{\ker \bar r}(\zeta_l) and F′ are linearly disjoint over ℚ. It justifies this by containment of that closure in F^{avoid} and the relation L′LF^{suff}(\zeta_N) ∩ F^{avoid} = …
sourceIssues.correction: Replace F′ by K = L′LF^{suff}(ζ_N). The sentence should read: "the Galois closure H of \overline{F}^{\ker\bar r}(ζ_l) over ℚ is linearly disjoint over ℚ from K = L′LF^{suff}(ζ_N)". K is Galois over ℚ, being the compositum of the Galois extensions L′, L, F^{suff} and ℚ(ζ_N). The displayed chain shows K ∩ F^{avoid} = ℚ, so K is linearly disjoint over ℚ from F^{avoid}, which contains H. Since F′ = FK, ACC+ Lemma 7.1.7 with E = K then shows that \bar r|_{G_{F′}} is absolutely irreducible and decomposed generic.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Lemma 2.3, final paragraph, first line of p. 1250 (the sentence begins "For the second condition, we" at the foot of p. 1249).
sourceIssues.printed: The source says the required check is N ∤ l^{r/2} − 1 = l^{2^{t_0−1} ∏_{i=1}^{m} p_i^{t_i}} − 1 when t_0 > 0.
sourceIssues.correction: need to verify that N ∤ l^{r/2} + 1 = l^{2^{t_0−1} ∏_{i=1}^{m} p_i^{t_i}} + 1. Both minus signs should be plus signs.
sourceIssues.reason: The second condition of Lemma 2.3 (p. 1248) says: when r is even, N ∤ l^{r/2} + 1. The final paragraph of the proof checks this condition. It sets out to prove it ("For the second condition, we need to verify that ..."), and both cases end with the plus sign. If m > 0, then M_1 divides l^{r/2} − 1 and M_1 is an odd divisor of N greater than 1, so "N ∤ l^{r/2} + 1". If m = 0, then N = M_0 = AB and r = 2^{t_0}, and by construction "M_0 = N ∤ l^{2^{t_0−1}} + 1". The target is printed with −1 in both places, and that is not the statement the proof needs. It is true, but it follows at once from the minimality of r, since r/2 < r. So the sign is a misprint. The intended statement is clear from the lemma, from the opening words of the sentence and from the two conclusions that follow, and the argument itself proves the plus-sign version. Neither the lemma nor the proof is affected. A minor point: the caveat "(if t_0 > 0)" is always satisfied, because the construction takes t_0 > 2, so r = 2^{t_0} ∏ p_i^{t_i} is always even. This sentence is not in arXiv v1. There, the proof of this condition simply reads "M_1 | l^{2^{t−1}∏ p_i^{t_i}} − 1 yields a contradiction with N | l^{r/2} + 1" (arXiv v1, p. 9). So the misprint entered when this paragraph was rewritten for publication.

sourceIssues.locator: Section 4, proof of Theorems 1.1 and 1.4, the paragraph after Proposition 4.1 beginning "On the side of characteristic l", p. 1270 (arXiv v1, p. 22, same wording, where Lemma 3.9 is numbered 3.8). It restates the third bullet of the choice of N at the start of Section 4, p. 1268.
sourceIssues.printed: The source includes the assumptions F_{l^2} ⊂ k(λ) and n | #(k(λ)^×).
sourceIssues.correction: Write n = l^a m with l ∤ m, as the paper does at the start of Section 4 (p. 1268). The sentence should read: "We also assumed that F_{l^2} ⊂ k(λ) and m | #(k(λ)^×)". Equivalently, k(λ) contains all n-th roots of unity in characteristic l, because μ_n(F̄_l) = μ_m. Nothing else changes: the x ↦ x^{l^a} map is a bijection on k(λ)^×, so (k(λ)^×)^n = (k(λ)^×)^m.
sourceIssues.reason: The group k(λ)^× is cyclic of order l^r − 1, which is prime to l. So the printed condition n | #(k(λ)^×) can hold only when l ∤ n. Take n = l = 3: then 3^r − 1 ≡ 2 mod 3 for every r. Theorem 1.1 allows l | n; it has no enormity hypothesis. (In Theorem 1.4 enormity forces l ∤ n, because when l | n the scalars have trace zero, so ad^0 has nonzero invariants.) So as printed, the sentence is false in some cases the theorem covers. It is also not what was assumed. The third bullet on p. 1268 requires F_{l^2}F' ⊂ F_l(ζ_N) = k(λ), where F' is generated by all m-th roots ("hence n-th roots") of elements of F_{l^s}. This gives the two facts the paragraph needs. (i) μ_m ⊂ k(λ). This is exactly the hypothesis of Lemma 2.1 that the finite field contains all n-th roots of unity. The proof of Lemma 2.1 on pp. 1244–1245 writes n = l^a m and uses the exact sequence with kernel Z/mZ, so it needs only this. (ii) Every element of F_{l^s} has an m-th root in k(λ), hence an n-th root in k(λ), since l^a-th powers are a bijection. So det r̄ takes values in (k(λ)^×)^n. The deduction from Lemma 3.9 uses only F_{l^2} ⊂ k(λ). Nowhere else is n | #(k(λ)^×) used; Lemma 3.7 and Proposition 3.8 involve only the order of l mod N. A small case confirms the corrected reading. For n = l = 3 we have m = 1, and the bullet asks for F_9F_{3^s} ⊂ F_3(ζ_N). Cubing is then an automorphism of k(λ)^×, and every k(λ)^×-valued character has a unique cube root. For n = 6, l = 3 the corrected condition 2 | 3^r − 1 always holds, while the printed 6 | 3^r − 1 never does. The intended meaning is clear from the paper's own set-up, and the argument is correct as intended. So this is a misprint (n for its prime-to-l part m) that affects nothing. It is not an error that affects the proof, as the original record said.
